title: McKinnon on why he scanned US military networks

tellings.quote: I read the disclosure project book Steven Greer and his team.

I thought I could use my basic networking skills just to do a scan, you know, a light scan on American military networks, which which is mad now, but but back then it was just kind of like a playful idea.
tellings.difference: Adds the method (blank passwords, a light scan) and the place (his girlfriend's aunt's house in London), and dates it 2000-2002.
tellings.link_reason: McKinnon scanning US military networks after reading the Disclosure Project book. This is the same account as the story about why he scanned those networks.

plain: Around 2000 to 2002, a British computer hacker named Gary McKinnon read a book from the Disclosure Project, a campaign led by Steven Greer and his team to gather testimony on hidden UFO knowledge, and decided to run what he calls "a light scan on American military networks" from his girlfriend's aunt's house in London. McKinnon tells Michels this himself. He says that by using accounts with blank passwords he got into networks at the National Security Agency at Fort Meade, the Defense Information Systems Agency, the Department of Defense, and the Army, Navy and Air Force, something he now calls "mad" but says felt at the time like "a playful idea" to see whether the book's claims held up.
